e.etymology: A spelling of Stewart, from Old English stigweard, the steward of a household. The High Stewards of Scotland became its royal house, and Mary, Queen of Scots, raised in France, adopted the French-style spelling.

assoc.t: House of Stuart, royal dynasty of Scotland and England
Stuart Little, E. B. White's mouse

e.etymology: A spelling of Ricky, the pet form of Richard. Richard is Germanic, from words for ruler and for hard or brave, and reached England with the Normans.
namesakes: Rickey Henderson (baseball's all-time stolen base leader)

assoc.t: rickey, a highball of gin or bourbon, lime and soda

e.etymology: A spelling of Devin or Devon. Devin comes from an Irish surname linked to words for poet or fawn; Devon is the English county. Deven is also a separate Indian name built on Sanskrit deva, god.
An American coinage of the early 1900s built on the La- prefix, the male counterpart of Lavonne. It is often written LaVon.
A spelling of Kaylee, a late 20th-century American combination of the sounds of Kay and Lee.
The stage name of R&B singer Omarion, born Omari Grandberry, who stretched Omari, the Swahili form of Omar, with an -on ending. US use peaked in 2005, the year of his solo debut.
A respelling of Chase, an English surname that began as a nickname for a hunter, from Old French chacier, to hunt.

assoc.t: sounds the same as Chase, the JPMorgan Chase consumer bank
sounds the same as Chase, the police pup in PAW Patrol

e.etymology: A respelling of Macy, a Norman surname from places called Massy in France, familiar to Americans from the department store. The May- spelling brings in May and Mae.

assoc.t: sounds like Macy's, the department store chain

e.etymology: From Hebrew Zakkai, pure or innocent, by way of Greek and Latin. In Luke's Gospel Zacchaeus is the short tax collector of Jericho who climbs a sycamore tree to see Jesus.
From Arabic sakina, the calm and peace of mind that the Quran describes God sending down on believers. Sakina bint Husayn, a great-granddaughter of the Prophet Muhammad, bore the name.
Reads as a spelling of Janie, the pet form of Jane, and matches the English surname Janney, from a medieval pet form of John.
namesakes: Allison Janney (Oscar-winning actress, The West Wing)

e.etymology: The Irish name Róisín without its accents: Róis, the Irish Rose, plus the diminutive -ín. Róisín Dubh, the Dark Little Rose, is a poetic name for Ireland from an old patriotic song.
e.note: Americans tend to read it as ROY-sin; the Irish say roh-SHEEN, so expect to correct people.

e.meaning: name of God, or God has heard
e.etymology: The Yiddish form of Shmuel, the Hebrew original of Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul and David. In the US it is used almost entirely in Hasidic communities.
From Arabic afnan, the plural of fanan, a branch. The word appears in the Quran's Surah ar-Rahman, describing the spreading branches of the gardens of paradise.
From Arabic hayah, life. It is a girls' name across the Arab world and Turkey, and in South Asia also a surname.
e.note: Americans tend to read it as HY-ut, the same as Hyatt, the hotel chain.

e.etymology: A pet form of Olivia, and sometimes of Livia. Olivia was popularized by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night and goes back to Latin oliva, olive.
A respelling of Jersey, the Channel Island and the state named for it, used as a place name like Dakota or Brooklyn. It is unrelated to Jerzy, the Polish form of George.

assoc.t: sounds like Jersey: New Jersey and the Jersey Shore
sounds like jersey, the sports shirt

e.etymology: From Sanskrit aruna, reddish, the color of the sky at daybreak. In Hindu myth Aruna is the charioteer who drives the sun god Surya; as a girls' name it is the feminine of Arun.

In Persian raha means free or released; in Arabic raha is rest and ease, a word Swahili borrowed for comfort and joy. Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Ranbir Kapoor gave the name to their daughter in 2022.
A new coinage that extends Ezra, Hebrew for help, with the -en ending of Owen and Soren.
A respelling of Savannah, from the Georgia city and its river, or from savanna, a grassy plain, a word English took from Spanish sabana, of Taino origin.

assoc.t: Savannah, Georgia, historic Southern port city

e.etymology: Two names share the spelling: Arabic kamal, perfection, used across the Muslim world (Kemal in Turkish), and Hindi kamal, lotus, from Sanskrit kamala, whose feminine is Kamala.

e.meaning: of Mars, the Roman god of war
e.etymology: A Roman family name, probably derived from Mars, made famous by the general Gaius Marius. It is common in France, Germany, Romania and Scandinavia.
namesakes: Marius Pontmercy (the young lover in Les Misérables)

assoc.t: Marius, Cosette's love in Les Misérables

e.etymology: From Sanskrit abhirama, pleasing or delightful, a word often applied to the gods Rama and Krishna.
The French-style spelling of Aisha, from Arabic for alive or living, the name of a wife of the Prophet Muhammad. This spelling is standard in North and West Africa and in France.
From Arabic tamim, complete or perfect, from the root for completion. Banu Tamim is one of the great Arab tribes, and Tamim al-Dari was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
A modern American coinage close to Amila and Amyra, with the look of Amy plus the -la ending of Myla and Kayla.
A respelling of Promise, the English word, from Latin promissum, a pledge. It belongs with modern word names like Journey and Destiny.

e.meaning: name of God, or God has heard
e.etymology: A pet form of Samuel for boys and Samantha for girls, also given as a full name. Samuel is Hebrew, read as name of God or God has heard.

assoc.t: sammie, casual slang for a sandwich

e.etymology: A variant of Kevin with the -von ending of Devon and Javon. Kevin comes from Irish Caoimhín, from words for gentle or handsome and birth.
A respelling of Cameron, the Scottish Highland clan name, from Gaelic cam, crooked, plus sron, nose. The -yn ending marks it as a girls' form.
